result.title: From 'polycrisis' to 'polytunity' - the future of geopolitics with Prof Yuen Yuen Ang
result.description:
"Polycrisis" was a term coined to describe the convergence of multiple global challenges: political polarisation, conflicts, and the breakdown of post-World War Two norms on issues such as trade and security.
Yuen Yuen Ang, a political science professor at Johns Hopkins University, says polycrisis was a useful way of framing the problem, but to find solutions we should consider the global "polytunity".
This episode of Radio Davos was produced jointly with CNA Correspondent from Singapore-based Channel News Asia, and is co-hosted with CNA journalist Olivia Siong. https://www.channelnewsasia.com/listen/cna-correspondent
This was recorded at the World Economic Forum’s Annual Meeting of the New Champions 2026. Catch up on that at wef.ch/amnc26 and across social media using the hashtag #AMNC26.

result.title: How to Face Uncertainty and Take Action: Lessons from a Blind Sailor's Pacific Crossing
result.description:
How can leaders move forward when pressure is high and the way is not clear? Blind adventurer Hiro Iwamoto and his ‘seeing eye Doug” crewmate Doug Smith sailed across the Pacific in 55 days, from San Diego to Fukushima. The two share key strategies for leaders in taking action despite uncertainty and what’s needed to pick the right partners to make impossible projects a reality. Hiro also shares how he stays calm in moments of extreme adversity, like when whale sank his boat during an earlier attempt leaving him in a life raft for 11 hours amid five-metre waves.
Key takeaways:

Courage means moving forward without waiting for 100% information.
Find people who can solve problems, not just point them out
How thinking in the present can prevent panic and enable decision-making
Hiro is an adventurer, keynote speaker and the first totally blind person to sail across the Pacific. Doug had no sailing experience but became Hiro’s crewmate and navigator for that extraordinary trip. Their lessons on crisis leadership, teamwork, overcoming fear and innovation can motivate any leader during difficult moments.

Recorded January 2026 at the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, Switzerland.

result.title: The Clean Energy Economy & What Is An AI-First Company? | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:12 - Clean energy is the economic story of the 21st century:
In today’s era of economic volatility and sluggish growth, the clean energy sector stands out as a global success story, creating jobs and driving economic growth around the world. China’s dominance in manufacturing has driven down the cost of solar panels and wind turbines, but its scale is causing smaller players to erect trade barriers as they try to compete, says Kelly Sims Gallagher, Dean of The Fletcher School. Healthy competition is good news for this sector’s future, she argues. But who will provide it? 

02.08 - What is an AI-first company?:
Plenty of companies are using artificial intelligence – but how many are AI-first? And what’s the difference? Here, Workera CEO Kian Katanforoosh talks us through the three levels of AI integration – AI-enabled, AI-first and AI-native – and explains how executives can better embed #AI in their own businesses. 

04.44 - How uncertainty taxes the modern economy:
"Policy uncertainty is acting as a drag on the global economy, says Paul Gruenwald, Global Chief Economist of S&P Global Ratings, as businesses and individuals hold back from spending because they don’t know what’s coming.

result.title: "Not just small men" - how healthcare is failing women, and what can be done
result.description:
Women spend 25% more of their lives in poor health than men and are 50% more likely to die of a heart attack than a male patient.
The statistics are staggering - but there are some relatively simple and cost-effective ways healthcare systems can improve the situation.
Lucy Perez of the McKinsey Health Institute sets out the challenges and talks us through these potential solutions.
